issues.description: The problem text (Part 2) requires a milk method messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) including a volume parameter and a specific return format with the volume, but the UML in the problem statement, the template usage, and the solution all define/expect messageOnMilk() with no parameters. This is an internal contradiction in the specification and a cross-artifact mismatch: students will not know whether to implement a no-arg messageOnMilk() or a messageOnMilk(double) with volume, and existing template/solution code (and example calls in Main) use the no-arg form.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the specification and code. Either (A) update the problem statement and UML to require messageOnMilk() with no parameters (and remove the volume requirement and example), or (B) change the interface and all implementations/calls to messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and adjust Main, template, and solution examples and tests to pass a volume. Prefer option B if tracking milk volume is intended: update Milkable to messageOnMilk(double), update Seal and Goat implementations to accept the volume and format the string as "[Animal Type] [name] is milked (volume: [milkVolume]L)", and update any example calls in Main and tests to provide a double argument.

issues.description: The problem statement contains conflicting specifications for the same conceptual method messageOnMilk: the UML and earlier parts define messageOnMilk() with no parameters, while Part 2's textual description requires messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) (including a volume in the return string). The template code (Main.java) and the solution repository define and call messageOnMilk() with no parameters. This mismatch in the method signature/contract is likely to confuse students about the required API and may cause compilation or implementation errors if they follow the textual description in Part 2.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent: either (A) update the problem statement text in Part 2 to require messageOnMilk() with no parameters and adjust the described return format to match the UML and solution (e.g., "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"), or (B) change the interface and all implementations (Milkable, Seal, Goat, and any calls) to messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and update template and solution code and examples accordingly. Prefer option A if the UML and template are authoritative to minimize changes.
